## Purpose

We want to know what cutoffs are likely appropriate to decide "good" (green), "be wary" (yellow) and "maybe don't use" (red) for some of the measures in our datasets.

So to do this, we summarized all the values across datasets 


```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 12,
  fig.height = 8,
  dev = c("ragg_png"),
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r}
#| label: targets
targets::tar_source(c("./packages.R", "R"))
tar_load(c(
  sets_percent_missing_result,
  sets_median_correlation_result,
  sets_rsd_result,
  sets_pc_number_result
))
```

## Percent Missing

What is the distribution of the percent missingness in the data?

```{r}
#| label: fig-percent-missing-all
#| fig-cap: All missingness values.
pm_all_plot = sets_percent_missing_result |>
  ggplot(aes(x = missing)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)
pm_all_plot
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-percent-missing-nozero
#| fig-cap: Missingness values > 0
sets_pm_n0 = sets_percent_missing_result |>
  dplyr::filter(missing > 0, !is.na(missing))
pm_n0_plot = sets_pm_n0 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = missing)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)
pm_n0_plot
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sd-missing
#| fig-cap: Missingness values > 0, with SD's marked at 1, 2,, 3 & 4.
missing_sd = sd(sets_pm_n0$missing)
pm_n0_sd_plot = sets_pm_n0 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = missing)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1, 2, 3, 4) * missing_sd, color = "red")
pm_n0_sd_plot
```

So, based on @fig-sd-missing, we could just use the SD value we have, and say 4 * SD (80), you are in the **red**.
Or we could argue an increment of 25 makes more sense, and do the 1, 2, and 3 * 25 cutoffs.
Either way seems like it would be fine.

## Median Correlations

```{r}
#| label: fig-median-cor-all
#| fig-cap: All median correlations across all datasets.
sets_median_correlation_result |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median_ici_correlation)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-median-cor-max
#| fig-cap: Maximum median correlation in each dataset.
sets_median_correlation_summary = sets_median_correlation_result |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    max = max(median_ici_correlation, na.rm = TRUE),
    min = min(median_ici_correlation, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = id
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.infinite(max), !is.infinite(min))
min_cor_plot = sets_median_correlation_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = min)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  labs(subtitle = "Minimum Correlations")
max_cor_plot = sets_median_correlation_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = max)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  labs(subtitle = "Maximum Correlations")
min_cor_plot / max_cor_plot
```

Looking at @fig-median-cor-max, I think we could evaluate the dataset as a whole, check the maximum observed, and if the maximum observed correlation falls below 0.5, that is something to flag.

```{r}
#| label: fig-median-cor-max-cutoffs
#| fig-cap: Where do different SD cutoffs lie on the maximum median correlation distribution?

summary_max_median_ici = tibble::tibble(
  median_value = median(sets_median_correlation_summary$max, na.rm = TRUE),
  sd_value = sd(sets_median_correlation_summary$max, na.rm = TRUE)
)

max_cor_plot +
  geom_vline(xintercept = summary_max_median_ici$median_value, color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = summary_max_median_ici$median_value -
      (c(2, 4) * summary_max_median_ici$sd_value),
    color = "red"
  )
```

## Relative Standard Deviations

```{r}
#| label: fig-rsd-all
#| fig-cap: All raw data median RSD values within subject-sample-factors, after filtering for values <= 3.
sets_rsd_result |>
  dplyr::filter(median <= 3) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-rsd-max-min
#| fig-cap: Histogram of minimum and maximum RSD values within experiments, after filtering for values <= 3.
sets_rsd_summary = sets_rsd_result |>
  dplyr::summarize(min = min(median), max = max(median), .by = id)
rsd_min_plot = sets_rsd_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(min <= 3) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = min)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  labs(subtitle = "Minimum RSD")
rsd_max_plot = sets_rsd_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(max <= 3) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = max)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  labs(subtitle = "Maximum RSD")
rsd_min_plot / rsd_max_plot
```

The overall distribution in @fig-rsd-all looks like the better one to use, so we will take it, and find the median value, and the SD's.

```{r}
#| label: fig-rsd-all-cutoffs
sets_rsd_stats = tibble::tibble(
  median = median(sets_rsd_result$median),
  sd = sd(sets_rsd_result$median)
)
rsd_cutoff_plot =
  sets_rsd_result |>
  dplyr::filter(median <= 3) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sets_rsd_stats$median, color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = sets_rsd_stats$median + (c(2, 4) * sets_rsd_stats$sd),
    color = "red"
  )
rsd_cutoff_plot
```

## PC That Captures 90% of Cumulative Variance

In @fig-pca-all, the log transformed PC-90 looks almost normal(ish).
What would the cutoffs be if we used this log-distribution to calculate a mean and SD??

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-all
#| fig-cap: PC number that represents cumulative 90% of variance, as a fraction of all the PCs calculated (left); as raw PC number (right), and log10(PC-N) (bottom). 

fraction_plot = sets_pc_number_result |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fraction_90)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)
pc_plot = sets_pc_number_result |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pc_90)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)
pc_log_plot = sets_pc_number_result |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log10(pc_90))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50)
(fraction_plot | pc_plot) / pc_log_plot
```

The only issue is, the mean, median and mode don't capture the central location that the eye does.
So I'm going with **0.5**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-cutoffs
#| fig-cap: Distribution and cutoffs if using a mode of 0.5.
sets_pc_number_result = sets_pc_number_result |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.infinite(pc_90)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(log_pc = log10(pc_90))
pc_summary_rmf = sets_pc_number_result |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    log_mode = 0.5,
    log_sd = sd(log_pc),
    sd_2 = log_mode + 2 * log_sd,
    sd_4 = log_mode + 4 * log_sd
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    tidyselect::everything(),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  )
pc_log_plot +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pc_summary_rmf$value[1], color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pc_summary_rmf$value[c(3, 4)], color = "red")
```

The cutoffs in normal values would correspond to:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pca-cutoffs
#| fig-cap: Values if using mode of 0.5
pc_summary_rmf |>
  dplyr::mutate(value_raw = 10^value) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(decimals = 2)
```


```{r}
#| label: fig-pca-cutoffs-real
#| fig-cap: Distribution and cutoffs if using the median as in all other datasets.
pc_summary = sets_pc_number_result |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    log_median = median(log_pc),
    log_sd = sd(log_pc),
    sd_2 = log_median + 2 * log_sd,
    sd_4 = log_median + 4 * log_sd
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    tidyselect::everything(),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "value"
  )
pc_log_plot +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pc_summary$value[1], color = "blue") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pc_summary$value[c(3, 4)], color = "red")
```

The cutoffs in normal values would correspond to:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pca-cutoffs-real
#| fig-cap: Values if using actual median.
pc_summary |>
  dplyr::mutate(value_raw = 10^value) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(decimals = 2)
```
